newsitem.title: CHINA: China to tighten control of state purchasing funds.
newsitem.headline: China to tighten control of state purchasing funds.

text.p: China has issued regulations to tighten control of funds used for state purchases of grain, cotton and oils, the People's Daily newspaper said on Saturday.

Under the rules issued by the People's Bank of China and the Ministry of Finance, officials at all levels would be required to ensure that state policy subsidies were properly allocated and banned from holding up funds sent by higher authorities, the newspaper said.

The regulations were aimed at stopping the loss of funds intended for use in state policy buying of agricultural products and would be backed by fines for offending officials, the People's Daily said.
The Agricultural Development Bank, its agents and other financial departments would be responsible for the adminstration and supervision of accounts used for purchase funds, it said.

Enterprises that received funds earmarked for state purchasing would not be allowed to use the money for anything else and would be required to keep it in an account at the Agricultural Development Bank of its agents, it said.
The People's Bank of China, the central bank, would oversee the Agricultural Development Bank role in ensuring purchase funds and subsidies were correctly managed, it said.
